title: Fix checklist step regressions caused by out-of-order onboarding events (ordering + idempotency)
creator: Leila Farouk
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description:
Dogfood bug: checklist step state can regress when onboarding events arrive out-of-order (or duplicated) across gateway/control-plane/backfill.

Impact
- Users see steps flip from Complete -> In progress / Not started after doing later steps.
- Support loses trust in checklist state; makes triage harder ("I already did this").
- Funnel/TTFS reporting gets noisy because derived completion timestamps move backwards.

Observed during dogfood
- Tenant: redwood-internal-devex (multiple testers)
- Steps affected (examples):
  - "Make your first successful API call" marked complete, then later becomes incomplete after a delayed API key creation event is ingested.
  - "Try streaming" completes, then "First successful request" shows incomplete because event ordering in the progress service applies last-write-wins to step state.

Root cause hypothesis
- Progress service currently computes step state as a direct function of the latest ingested event per step and applies updates in ingest order.
- Events are emitted from multiple producers (API gateway + control plane), and occasionally arrive late due to retries/queue delays.
- Backfill job can write historical events (or synthetic completion) after real-time events have already been processed.
- Dedupe/idempotency key is not consistently enforced; duplicate emissions can re-trigger transitions and re-compute derived timestamps.

Repro (internal)
1) Create API key (control plane emits onboarding.api_key.created)
2) Immediately run a request using streaming quickstart (gateway emits onboarding.request.first_2xx + onboarding.streaming.first_established)
3) Force delay in control plane emitter (or replay from staging SQS) so api_key.created is delivered after streaming events
4) Observe checklist: steps briefly show correct completion, then regress after delayed api_key.created ingestion triggers re-evaluation.

Expected behavior
- Checklist step transitions must be monotonic within a tenant and checklist version: Not started -> In progress -> Complete. Never regress due to late/duplicate events.
- For steps computed from events, completion timestamp should be the earliest valid observed event time (event_occurred_at), not ingestion time.

Proposed fix
A) Event-level idempotency + dedupe
- Require an idempotency_key for write path (even internal) and dedupe at ingestion:
  - idempotency_key = tenant_id + event_name + source + source_event_id (or request_id for gateway)
- Reject or no-op duplicates; log a counter for visibility.

B) Ordering / monotonic application
- Store step completion fields as "first_completed_at" per step and only set them if null OR if incoming event_occurred_at is earlier than the currently stored value.
- Do not clear completion fields during recompute.
- Treat derived state as: complete if first_completed_at != null.

C) Separate "event_occurred_at" from "ingested_at"
- Use event_occurred_at for step completion and TTFS/TTFP; retain ingested_at only for debugging.
- Guardrails: if event_occurred_at is missing/invalid, fallback to ingested_at but never regress a completed step.

D) Regression tests
- Unit tests: simulate out-of-order ingest across 3 events and ensure step state stays Complete.
- Integration test: replay a small fixture in random order; assert final state.

E) Observability
- Emit metric: checklist_progress.out_of_order_event (counter) when an event_occurred_at < latest_seen_event_occurred_at for tenant.
- Add data quality check in KPI pipeline: step completion timestamps should be non-decreasing across dependent steps (soft check; alert on spikes).

Acceptance criteria
- In dogfood tenant, no step regressions after 24h with repeated replay/retries.
- Support/admin override remains functional (manual mark complete should not be overwritten by later events).
- Backfill job can run after real-time events without changing completed steps (except to set earlier timestamps when missing).
- Dashboard TTFS/TTFP values stable pre/post replays; no negative deltas.

References
- Related: ENG-5813 (progress service), ENG-5844 (backfill), PM-751 (metric definition)
- PR target: redwood/pr-28510-fix-checklist-state-race-condition

Notes / trade-offs
- This fix prioritizes monotonic correctness over strict "truth" if we later decide to remove a step definition; step versioning should handle that separately (not in scope here).
- If we accept backfill events with earlier timestamps, that may change TTFS slightly (earlier), which is desirable for correctness but should be called out to KPI owners.
comments: 2025-03-19 — Leila Farouk: Found during E2E dogfood run. Steps 2 and 4 flipped back to incomplete after a delayed control-plane event. Attaching HAR + screenshots in Drive (link in Console dogfood notes).

2025-03-20 — Logan Wright: +1 this matches what we see in telemetry pipeline when the gateway retries event emission on timeout; duplicates arrive minutes later. We should treat progress updates as idempotent and step transitions as monotonic. Also please avoid any per-event recompute that can clear fields.

2025-03-21 — Jada Williams: Suggest storing per-step first_completed_at and never clearing it. If we need to support "reset" later, that should be an explicit admin action with audit trail, not an event side-effect.
2025-03-24 — Chloe Martin: Implementing in progress-service: added idempotency_key enforcement + unique index; changed reducer to set first_completed_at only. Adding randomized-order fixture test.
2025-03-26 — Chris Osei: For TTFS/TTFP, please ensure we use event_occurred_at. If missing, fallback should not create backwards jumps; document in metrics definition ticket.

2025-03-28 — Chloe Martin: PR up: sources/github/redwood/pr-28510-fix-checklist-state-race-condition.json. Includes unit tests and a migration to backfill missing idempotency_key for internal producers (gateway already has request_id).
2025-04-02 — Leila Farouk: Verified in dogfood: replayed events in reversed order 10x; no regressions. Also confirmed admin override (mark complete) persists after replays.
2025-04-03 — Dylan Brooks: Marking done. Please keep an eye on out_of_order_event metric during cohort rollout; if it spikes, we may need producer-side batching/flush tuning.
